questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates knowledge of persistent data structures, rope-based string representations, and efficient substring hashing under versioning—skills directly applicable to building collaborative text editors.

## Key Concepts
- **Persistent data structures with path-copying**: Each modification creates new nodes along the affected path while sharing unchanged subtrees with previous versions
- **Rope implementation**: Balanced BST enabling O(log n) split and concatenate operations
- **Subtree aggregates**: Cached length and rolling hash enable O(log n) substring queries
- **Memory considerations**: Path-copying creates O(log n) new nodes per edit; total memory grows proportionally with edit count, though unused nodes can be garbage collected
- **Collision handling**: Use a polynomial rolling hash with large prime modulus; combine with second hash function (e.g., MD5 or SHA prefix) for verification in critical applications
- **Balancing and concatenation**: Treap balancing (via randomized priorities) maintains O(log n) operations; concatenation merges two trees by attaching the smaller as a child of the larger, or by creating a new root with both as children

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests time-window dynamic data with multi-key aggregates and top-k queries, challenging both data layout and lazy deletions.

## Key Concepts
- Time-window maintenance with insertions and deletions
- Per-user aggregate tracking for top-k queries
- Per-service latency distribution for kth-largest queries

## Code Example
```javascript
class LogStore {
  insertLog(userId, serviceId, timestamp, latency) {
    // Add to global treap by timestamp; update per-user and per-service structures
  }
  eraseLogsInTimeWindow(start, end) {
    // Mark logs in [start, end] as deleted; adjust aggregates lazily
  }
}
```

## Data Structures
- **Global treap**: Time-ordered logs for window queries
- **Per-user trees**: Track total latency by user for top-k
- **Per-service trees**: Maintain latency distribution for kth-largest
- **Lazy deletion**: Mark invalid entries, clean during queries

## Update Rules
- Insert: Update all structures in O(log n)
- Delete: Mark as deleted, defer cleanup
- Query: Verify consistency, trigger cleanup if needed

## Edge Cases
- Duplicate timestamps: Use secondary key (userId, serviceId)
- Empty windows: Return empty results
- Large deletions: Batch cleanup to maintain performance
